# Anthony Pye

## Overview

- **Age:** School-age child (under nine or ten)  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016)</sub>
- **Status:** Student  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolboy  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>

## Appearance

Anthony is a small boy with a pointed, freckled face, dark sullen eyes, and a sullen or defiant facial expression. He is part of the Pye family, whose members are described as having a family resemblance in temperament.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P55](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0055), [v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c15 P26](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0026), [v1 c17 P33](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0033)_

## Personality

Anthony is sullen, defiant, and stubbornly independent, refusing to yield easily to authority. He holds a firm prejudice against female teachers, believing them to be 'no good.' Despite his antagonistic and rebellious attitude in school, he possesses an underlying sense of respect when confronted directly, showing that he can acknowledge a rival or authority figure who stands up to him.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c17 P28](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0028), [v1 c17 P33](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0033), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036)_

## Traits

- Sullen and defiant  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- Prejudiced against female teachers  <sub>[v1 c17 P28](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0028), [v1 c17 P33](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0033)</sub>
- Stubborn and independent  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036)</sub>

## History

Anthony Pye attended the Avonlea school under the instruction of Mr. Phillips and later Miss Muriel Stacy. When Anne Shirley began teaching at Avonlea, Anthony showed a distinct prejudice against her, declaring that girl teachers were 'no good.' Throughout the term, he exhibited a sullen and rebellious attitude in the classroom, frequently mocking Anne or resisting her authority. After Anne lost her temper and cracked a slate over Gilbert Blythe's head, and later when she punished Anthony, his attitude subtly shifted; he began to respect Anne's determination and ability to hold her own, eventually acknowledging her academic and personal rivalry with Gilbert.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c15 P38](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0038), [v1 c17 P28](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0028), [v1 c17 P33](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0033), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036)_
